public_rationale: The testable part of this claim is the forecast that generative AI 'won't do much more than it can do now' (December 2024). A decisive later event contradicts it. In July 2025, IMO coordinators officially graded a Gemini Deep Think model at gold-medal level: it solved five of six problems in natural language within contest time. The year before, Google needed specialized formal systems, manual translation and up to three days to reach silver. METR also measured the length of tasks AI models can complete doubling about every seven months, a trend that held for models released after the post. The 'over-leveraged' part has no stated measure and is not scored.
limitations: The IMO result is cited through a secondary blog that quotes DeepMind and Hassabis, because the primary page would not load.
'Much more' is a judgment, and the speaker might argue that benchmark or contest gains are not useful capabilities.
The 'over-leveraged' half of the sentence is not assessed.

statement.excerpt: The tech industry is over-leveraged, having doubled, tripled, quadrupled down on generative AI — a technology that doesn't do much more than it did a few months ago and won't do much more than it can do now.

our_interpretation: The testable core is the forecast that generative AI 'won't do much more than it can do now', with December 2024 as the baseline.

Plain reading: no major new capability beyond December 2024 frontier models. A clear, independently verified jump on a hard task that frontier models could not do in December 2024 would contradict it.
'Over-leveraged' is a vague financial characterization with no stated measure, so it is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Through the evaluation date, generative AI models show no major capability beyond what December 2024 frontier models could do, on independent evaluations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After December 3, 2024, generative AI models show an independently verified capability clearly beyond December 2024 models, such as gold-medal performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad or large measured gains in autonomous task length.

evidence.locator: Update section, quote from Demis Hassabis
evidence.explanation: In July 2025, IMO coordinators officially graded a generative AI model at gold-medal level. This is a verified capability no generative AI model had in December 2024.

evidence.excerpt: scoring gold with a single model, within the allotted time and with no manual step to translate the problems first
evidence.explanation: Sets the baseline: the 2024 result needed specialized formal systems, manual translation and days of compute. The 2025 result came from a natural-language model within contest time.

evidence.excerpt: the length of tasks models can complete is well predicted by an exponential trend, with a doubling time of around 7 months.
evidence.explanation: An independent evaluator measured continued rapid growth in the length of tasks models can complete, including models released after December 2024.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: An officially certified IMO gold-medal score by a generative AI model after December 3, 2024, which no generative AI model had achieved by December 2024.
